text: dsh-mac-use 是面向 DeepSeek Harness Desktop 的 macOS 桌面操作插件，向 agent 提供观察屏幕、读取辅助功能界面树和执行鼠标键盘操作的工具。它通过工具接口读取显示器、窗口与光标信息，支持截图、打开应用或 URL、点击、拖动、滚动、输入文字和按键组合。适合需要让 DSH agent 在本机应用或浏览器中完成界面任务的用户；使用前需授予 Harness 屏幕录制与辅助功能权限，并可调整操作延迟和虚拟光标设置。

dsh-mac-use adds macOS desktop tools to DeepSeek Harness. Agents can inspect windows, read Accessibility trees, capture screenshots, open apps, and control mouse and keyboard. Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions are required.
想让 DSH agent 帮我操作 macOS 桌面应用。
有没有办法让 agent 看见屏幕并点击界面？
我想让模型读取应用的辅助功能界面树，不依赖截图。
让 DSH 自动输入文字、按快捷键并滚动窗口。
I want a DSH agent to inspect and operate apps on my Mac.
Can an agent read an app UI tree and click controls on screen?
dsh-mac-use 的功能「屏幕与窗口观察」：computer_screen_info 返回显示器尺寸、光标位置和屏幕窗口列表，帮助 agent 确定全局坐标。
dsh-mac-use 的功能「读取辅助功能界面树」：computer_ax_snapshot 按应用名称或 bundle id 读取 macOS AX 层级、文本和坐标，并限制遍历规模。
dsh-mac-use 的功能「截图并提供坐标映射」：computer_screenshot 可截取主屏、指定区域、窗口或显示器，并返回图片及像素到屏幕点的比例。
dsh-mac-use 的功能「鼠标与滚动操作」：agent 可按全局坐标移动、点击、拖动或在指定位置滚动，也可使用虚拟光标。
dsh-mac-use 的功能「输入文字与按键组合」：computer_type 将 Unicode 文本输入当前焦点，computer_key 支持字母、方向键和修饰键组合。
dsh-mac-use 仅面向 macOS 上运行的 DeepSeek Harness Desktop；截图需要屏幕录制权限，辅助功能读取和鼠标键盘操作需要 Accessibility 权限。
DSH 能帮我截取某个窗口并据图定位按钮吗？
I need an agent to launch an app and enter text using keyboard shortcuts.
dsh-mac-use README · Introduction：<div align="center">

dsh-mac-use README · dsh-mac-use：**Computer-use for DeepSeek Harness on macOS.** Let an agent _see_ the screen, _drive_ the mouse and keyboard, and _open_ apps and URLs — the same observe → act → verify loop as Claude's `computer` tool or Codex computer-use, shipped as a single DeepSeek Harness bundle. [](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-mac-use) [](LICENSE) [-lightgrey>)](#) [](#) [](https://github.com/matyik/dsh-mac-use/releases)

dsh-mac-use README · Why：Most computer-use setups ship a separate helper binary that needs its own screen-recording
and accessibility grants. `dsh-mac-use` doesn't:

dsh-mac-use README · Why：- **Plugin only, no extra binary.** Everything runs inside the DeepSeek Harness Desktop
  host process. Screen capture uses the bundled `screencapture` tool; mouse/keyboard and
  window inspection call macOS APIs through the `koffi` FFI library (an npm dependency).
- **Permissions come from the Harness app itself.** Because the plugin runs in the Desktop
  host (a child of the Electron app), macOS checks Screen Recording and Accessibility
  against _DeepSeek Harness_. Grant those two once — never to a helper.
- **Virtual agent cursor.** Mouse actions don't strand your real pointer: clicks land,
  then your cursor snaps back, while a blue arrow (white outline, ~2x size) glides between
  action points with its tip on the exact target — and it disappears when the task is done.

dsh-mac-use README · Tools：| Tool                   | What it does                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `computer_screenshot`  | Capture the screen (main display, a region, a window, or a display) and return the image plus bounds and pixel→point scale.                   |
| `computer_screen_info` | Read display geometry (points), cursor position, and the on-screen window list (id, app, title, bounds).                                      |
| `computer_ax_snapshot` | Read an app's Accessibility (AX) UI tree as compact text — roles, titles, values, and screen-coordinate frames, each with an integer `[ref]`. |
| `computer_move`        | Move the **agent cursor** to `(x, y)` in global display points (your real pointer is untouched).                                              |
| `computer_click`       | Click at `(x, y)` — left/right/middle, single or double.

dsh-mac-use README · Tools：A system-prompt section teaches the agent the workflow: observe → locate → convert image
pixels to global points → act → screenshot again to verify.

dsh-mac-use README · Accessibility snapshots：- **Cheap and text-only.** A snapshot is a few hundred tokens and readable by any model —
  no vision required.
- **Screen coordinates.** Each `@{x,y,w,h}` frame is in global display points, top-left
  origin — the same space as `computer_move` / `computer_click`.
- **Refs.** The `[n]` index on each line is stable for that snapshot; a later phase will
  accept a ref to act on the element directly.
- **Bounded.** It walks to `maxDepth` (default 8), visits up to `maxNodes` (default 300)
  nodes, caps the text at `maxChars` (default 12,000), and stops after ~1.5 s so an
  unresponsive app can't freeze the agent. When it stops early, `truncated` is `true` and
  the text ends with a `… N more nodes not shown` line.

dsh-mac-use README · Requirements：- **DeepSeek Harness Desktop** (the macOS app), running on macOS (Apple Silicon).
- A **vision-capable model** for full observe-and-act (e.g. `deepseek-flash`, which reads
  images). Text-only models can still use `computer_ax_snapshot`, `computer_screen_info`,
  and the action tools.

dsh-mac-use README · Permissions (once)：1. **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen Recording** → enable **DeepSeek Harness**.
2. **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility** → enable **DeepSeek Harness**
   (needed for mouse/keyboard input).
3. Fully quit and reopen DeepSeek Harness.

Missing a permission? The relevant tool fails with a message naming the exact setting.

dsh-mac-use README · Install：Install through the built-in Plugin Manager — no shell commands, no manual profile edits.

**From npm (recommended):**

```
dsh-mac-use
```

**From git:**

```
github:matyik/dsh-mac-use
```

In the Web sidebar: **Plugins → Install bundle**, enter either spec above (or a local
directory). The `plugin_manager` tool's `install_bundle` accepts the same targets.

dsh-mac-use README · Install：The only dependency is `koffi@3.1.1` (the version the Desktop runtime ships). It bundles a
prebuilt `darwin-arm64` binary and its install script is a fast prebuild check — no
compilation. pnpm 11 may ask you to approve that script once: click **Allow these scripts
and retry** and it finishes instantly.

dsh-mac-use README · Coordinate system：All mouse coordinates are **global display points**, origin at the top-left of the main
display (the same space as `computer_screen_info` and the click tools). Screenshots are
returned in **device pixels**, so `computer_screenshot` also reports `bounds` (points) and
`scale` (image pixels per point):

```
x = bounds.x + px / scale
y = bounds.y + py / scale
```

dsh-mac-use README · Configuration：| Field           | Default | Meaning                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `virtualCursor` | `true`  | Use the virtual agent cursor (click, then restore your pointer) and show the blue arrow. Set `false` to leave the pointer where it clicked. |
| `postDelayMs`   | `25`    | Delay between press/release events.                                                                                                         |
| `scrollAmount`  | `3`     | Scroll wheel units per step.                                                                                                                |
| `typeDelayMs`   | `0`     | Per-character typing delay.                                                                                                                 |

dsh-mac-use README · Security：These tools drive the real desktop — treat them as powerful. They run under the agent's
normal permission/approval policy; keep them in a preset that prompts before acting, and
have the agent re-check its work with a follow-up screenshot. macOS-only: on other
platforms the tools register but error when called.
